title: Private Deployments: VPC & On-Prem Reference Architectures, Packaging, Day-2 Ops, Upgrade & Rollback, Customer Requirements Library
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview:

This consolidated reference covers Redwood Inference private deployments (VPC and on-prem). It combines reference architectures, packaging guidance, day-2 operational procedures, upgrade and rollback playbooks, and a customer requirements library. Audience: SREs, platform engineers, solutions architects, and customer success engineers supporting enterprise/private deployments.

Sections in this page:
1) Summary and goals
2) Reference architectures (VPC and on-prem)
3) On-prem packaging and deployment artifacts
4) Day-2 operations (monitoring, maintenance, scaling)
5) Upgrade and rollback procedures
6) Customer requirements library (checklists & templates)
7) Ownership, SLAs and runbook links
8) Appendix: example configs and CLI snippets

1) Summary and goals
- Goal: Provide repeatable, secure, and observable private deployments that meet enterprise requirements for data residency, network isolation, and predictable inference economics.
- Scope: Multi-AZ VPC deployments on major cloud providers and air-gapped on-prem bundles (container images, Helm charts, packaging).
- Non-goals: Deep provider-specific networking tutorials (refer to vendor docs). This document focuses on Redwood's recommended patterns and artifacts.

2) Reference architectures
2.1 VPC Reference architecture (recommended for medium enterprise)
- Logical components:
  - Control plane: either Redwood-managed control plane (private control plane model) or customer-managed control plane for fully private deployments.
  - Data plane: GPU model serving clusters, autoscaler control plane, KV cache store, metrics/telemetry forwarders, and ingress gateways.
  - Network: private subnets per AZ, NAT for controlled outbound updates, bastion/jump host in management subnet, and VPC endpoints for S3/KMS where applicable.
- Typical instance sizing (starting point):
  - Small: 4 x A10G-equivalent GPUs, 2x small management nodes, 1x Redis cache (r5.large).
  - Medium: 8-16 x A100/RTX6000-equivalent GPUs, 3 control plane nodes, dedicated logging/monitoring nodes.
  - Large: scale GPU nodes in ASGs with instance types matching performance profile (NVLink topologies as required).
- Sizing rules of thumb:
  - Target p95 latency for <=256-token completions: <150ms for Platinum tier; use batching and cache to meet cost targets.
  - CPU:GPU ratio: recommend minimum 8 vCPUs per GPU for kernel scheduling and IO.

2.2 On-prem reference architecture (air-gapped or private data center)
- Logical components:
  - Kubernetes cluster (preferred) or bare-metal service groupings.
  - Dedicated GPU node pool.
  - Storage: NFS or CSI for model artifacts; optional local NVMe for model cache.
  - Optional hardware HSM/KMS appliance for key management.
- Networking:
  - Separate management VLAN from inference VLAN.
  - Firewall rules: allow only control plane CIDR and admin workstations to management endpoints.
- HA and fault domains:
  - Spread GPU nodes across racks/power domains where possible.
  - Control plane: 3-node quorum for control components; etcd replication for stateful components.

2.3 Deployment topologies and routing
- Multi-AZ VPC with cross-AZ load balancing for redundancy.
- Active/active model serving with regional failover via DNS policies.
- Graceful degradation: fallback to quantized/lower-capacity model variants when capacity constrained.

3) On-prem packaging and deployment artifacts
- Artifact types provided by Redwood:
  - Docker images (signed, versioned): redwood/inference:v{MAJOR}.{MINOR}.{PATCH}
  - Helm charts (templated values.yaml) for Kubernetes installs
  - TAR bundles for air-gapped installs (images + Helm + airgap installer)
  - Signed manifests and checksums (SHA256) with a release manifest file for verification

3.1 Packaging requirements and signing
- Images and charts are signed using Redwood's Notary/GPG pipeline; customers must verify signatures before deployment.
- Release manifest example (text):
  - release_version: 2026.05.22
  - images: [redwood/inference:v2026.05.22, redwood/runtime:v3.4.1]
  - checksums: images: sha256:<hash>, helm: sha256:<hash>
- Airgap bundle contents: images.tar.gz, charts.tgz, installer.sh, release_manifest.yaml, signatures.sig

3.2 Packaging checklist for on-prem delivery
- Confirm GPU drivers and supported CUDA versions (see compatibility table in appendix).
- Confirm node labeling and taints for inference workloads.
- Verify firewall, DNS, and NTP configuration on all nodes.
- Verify HSM/KMS connectivity and certificate thumbprints if using customer-managed keys.

4) Day-2 operations (monitoring, maintenance, scaling)
4.1 Observability and telemetry
- Metrics to collect: per-model token throughput, p50/p95/p99 latency, GPU utilization, GPU memory usage, cache hit rate, and request error rate.
- Recommended dashboards: per-model latency and cost, per-route error attribution, and system capacity utilization.
- Logging: structured JSON logs including request_id, model_version, route, user_tier; forward to customer SIEM or Redwood logging endpoints as configured.

4.2 Alerts and SLOs
- Example customer-default SLOs:
  - Availability: 99.95% (monthly) for Dedicated/private control plane connectivity.
  - Latency: p95 < 250ms for <=512-token requests (workload-dependent).
  - Error budget policy: sustained degradation for 14 days triggers auto-escalation.
- Example alert thresholds:
  - GPU OOM rate > 1% over 5m => P1
  - Serving error rate > 0.5% over 5m => P1
  - Cache hit rate < 30% for 30m on high-QPS routes => P2

4.3 Routine maintenance and scaling
- Maintenance windows: schedule kernel and driver patches in designated windows; use rolling restart plan and prewarm nodes after restarts.
- Scaling: prefer autoscaler for cloud; for on-prem, maintain warm standby nodes and follow a horizontal scale plan to avoid long ramp times.

5) Upgrade and rollback procedures
5.1 Upgrade strategy
- Canary rollout flow: 5% traffic to new revision for 30 minutes with synthetic test prompts. If no regressions, increase to 25% for 60 minutes, then proceed to full rollout.
- Validation during canary: functional smoke tests, latency/throughput regressions, crash/error monitoring, and model output QA checks against golden prompt set.

5.2 Pre-upgrade checklist
- Backup critical configs: export Helm values, take PV snapshots, and save etcd snapshot for control plane.
- Verify node health and drain non-GPU nodes for control plane upgrades first.
- Confirm rollback image and manifest are available and verified.

5.3 Step-by-step upgrade procedure (Kubernetes + Helm)
1) Prepare: export current Helm values and create snapshots:
   kubectl get configmap redwood-values -n redwood -o yaml > redwood-values-<date>.yaml
   ETCD snapshot: etcdctl snapshot save snapshot-<date>.db
2) Apply canary: update Helm release with canary flags and weight:
   helm upgrade redwood ./charts/redwood --namespace redwood -f redwood-values-<date>.yaml --set image.tag=v<release> --set canary.enabled=true --set canary.weight=5
3) Run synthetic tests for 30 minutes (see appendix).
4) If pass, increase weight to 25% and observe for 60 minutes.
5) If pass, complete rollout to 100% and remove canary settings.

5.4 Rollback procedure
- If failure detected at any stage:
  1) Stop traffic to canary by setting canary.weight=0 or reverting traffic policy.
  2) Roll back Helm release to previous revision: helm rollback redwood <previous_revision> --namespace redwood.
  3) If stateful DB compatibility issue suspected, restore etcd snapshot and restart services in controlled order.
  4) Open incident, run postmortem, and notify oncall.

6) Customer requirements library (templates & checklists)
- Network & security checklist (customer fills):
  - CIDR allocations for control and data plane subnets.
  - Outbound egress policy (allowed hosts/ports).
  - Firewall rules for bastion and admin access.
  - KMS/HSM endpoint details and certificate thumbprints.
  - SIEM/syslog endpoint and retention policy.

- Hardware & capacity checklist:
  - GPU types, counts, and expected QPS per model.
  - Host OS and kernel version requirements.
  - Storage: expected model sizes and cold/warm cache strategy.

- Compliance checklist:
  - Data residency and encryption at rest (AES-256).
  - TLS versions for in-transit encryption and mutual TLS where required.
  - Audit log retention period and access control requirements.

- Customer deliverables and handoff items:
  - Signed network diagram, approved IP ranges, and admin contact list.
  - Access credentials for deployment windows (time-boxed) and pre-agreed rollback windows.

7) Ownership, SLAs and runbook links
- Ownership summary:
  - Engineering (eng-private-deployments): packaging, release artifacts, major release orchestration.
  - Customer Success & Solutions Engineering: onboarding, runbook handover, and acceptance testing.
  - Customer: cluster administration, network configuration, and hardware provisioning.
- Runbooks and related pages:
  - /confluence/eng-private-deployments/private-deployments-vpc-onprem-deployment-runbook-2026-03-01
  - /confluence/eng-private-deployments/private-deployments-vpc-onprem-deployment-and-day2-guide-2026-07-20

8) Appendix: example configs and CLI snippets
- Example Helm values (snippet):
  replicaCount: 3
  image:
    repository: redwood/inference
    tag: v2026.05.22
  resources:
    requests:
      cpu: 8000m
      memory: 32Gi
    limits:
      cpu: 16000m
      memory: 64Gi
  nodeSelector:
    accelerator: nvidia-tesla-a100

- Example airgap deploy command (customer run):
  sh installer.sh --bundle /tmp/redwood-airgap-2026.05.22.tar.gz --kubeconfig /home/admin/.kube/config --accept-licence

- Synthetic test script (basic):
  #!/bin/bash
  set -e
  ENDPOINT=https://internal-redwood.example.local/v1/generate
  for i in {1..100}; do
    curl -s -X POST "$ENDPOINT" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{\"prompt\":\"The quick brown fox\",\"max_tokens\":16}' | jq . >> /tmp/synth.out || exit 1
  done
  # Use customer tooling to compute p95 and error rate from /tmp/synth.out

Compatibility table (high level):
- CUDA: supported 11.7, 11.8
- NVIDIA drivers: 525.x - 535.x recommended
- Kubernetes: 1.25 - 1.27 supported; 1.28+ requires validation
